manufacturing.cutting_speed.title: Machining (cutting) speed from spindle speed and diameter

variables.name: omega
variables.desc: spindle angular speed (enter rpm or rps)
variables.label: ω

assumptions: v = ω·D/2 uses ω in rad/s directly; there is no extra 2π for an rpm entry (1000 rpm = 104.72 rad/s).

manufacturing.feed_rate.title: Machining feed rate from feed per revolution and spindle speed

variables.name: f
variables.desc: feed per revolution of the spindle

variables.name: n
variables.desc: spindle speed in revolutions per second (1500 rpm = 25 1/s)

assumptions: n is cyclic (rev/s): enter Hz, 1/s or 1/min, not rpm (pint treats rpm as angular and the core refuses the mix-up). Divide rpm by 60 to get rev/s.
method_references: Feed rate = feed per revolution × spindle speed (recalled)

manufacturing.milling_feed_rate.title: Milling table feed rate from feed per tooth

variables.name: f_z
variables.desc: feed per tooth (chip load per tooth)

variables.name: z
variables.desc: number of teeth on the cutter

variables.name: n
variables.desc: spindle speed in revolutions per second (1500 rpm = 25 1/s)

assumptions: Milling feed rate = feed per tooth × number of teeth × spindle rev/s (f_z·z·N). Distinct from turning, where the feed is already per revolution.

manufacturing.mrr.title: Material removal rate (turning)
assumptions: Turning MRR = v·f·d (the swept chip area is f·d).

manufacturing.milling_mrr.title: Material removal rate (milling)
assumptions: Milling MRR = table feed rate × radial engagement × axial depth (the swept chip area is a_e·a_p).

manufacturing.drilling_mrr.title: Material removal rate (drilling)
assumptions: Drilling MRR = hole area (πD²/4) × axial feed rate.

manufacturing.machining_time.title: Machining time for a straight cut
assumptions: One pass at constant spindle speed; feed per revolution × rev/s = linear feed rate.

manufacturing.cutting_force_power.title: Cutting force and machining power from specific cutting energy

variables.name: u
variables.desc: specific cutting energy (material constant, e.g. Kienzle)

assumptions: u is the specific cutting energy (energy per unit volume, a material input); F_c = u·(chip area f·d).

manufacturing.chip_thickness_ratio.title: Chip thickness ratio (undeformed / actual chip thickness)
assumptions: r < 1 because the chip is thicker than the undeformed layer (r = 1 only for no shear).

manufacturing.shear_angle_merchant.title: Shear plane angle from the chip thickness ratio (Merchant geometry)
assumptions: Geometric relation between the rake angle and the chip ratio; α positive as drawn.
method_references: tan φ = r cos α / (1 − r sin α) (Merchant, recalled)

manufacturing.merchant_friction_angle.title: Merchant circle friction angle and coefficient

variables.name: beta
variables.desc: friction angle on the rake face
variables.label: β

variables.name: mu
variables.desc: mean friction coefficient on the rake face
variables.label: μ

assumptions: Forces resolved on the rake face: F = F_c sin α + F_t cos α, N = F_c cos α − F_t sin α, μ = F/N. Requires N > 0.
method_references: Merchant force circle, μ = (F_c sin α + F_t cos α)/(F_c cos α − F_t sin α) (recalled)

manufacturing.taylor_tool_life.title: Taylor tool life equation (V·Tⁿ = constant)

variables.name: V1
variables.desc: cutting speed at tool life T1

variables.name: T1
variables.desc: tool life at cutting speed V1

variables.name: T2
variables.desc: tool life at cutting speed V2

assumptions: V·Tⁿ = C is constant, so one known (V1, T1) point plus the exponent n predicts T2 at V2 (T2 = T1·(V1/V2)^(1/n)). C itself is a material/tool input recovered from the data point.

manufacturing.surface_roughness.title: Ideal turned-surface roughness from feed and nose radius
assumptions: Ideal (geometric) profile only, R_a ≈ f²/(32 r_n) and R_t ≈ f²/(8 r_n); real finish is rougher (built-up edge, vibration, feed marks).
method_references: Ideal surface roughness R_a = f²/(32·r_n), R_t = f²/(8·r_n) (recalled)

manufacturing.grinding.title: Grinding wheel speed and material removal rate
assumptions: MRR = workpiece speed × depth of cut × width; wheel speed v_s = ω_s·D_s/2 (no hidden 2π).
method_references: Grinding MRR = v_w·d·b; wheel speed v_s = ω_s·D_s/2 (recalled)

manufacturing.rolling_force.title: Flat rolling force, contact length, draft and roll pressure

variables.name: p
variables.desc: mean roll pressure F/(w·L) (= average flow stress in this model)

assumptions: No friction-hill correction (p = σ_f); hf ≤ h0 required.
method_references: Rolling force F = w·σ_f·√(R·Δh); contact length L = √(R·Δh) (recalled)

manufacturing.rolling_max_draft.title: Maximum draft for roll bite (friction limit)

variables.name: mu
variables.desc: friction coefficient between roll and strip
variables.label: μ

assumptions: Bite condition tan α ≤ μ with Δh ≈ R·tan²α gives Δh_max = μ²R (small-angle form).

manufacturing.flow_stress.title: Flow stress from the power-law (Hollomon) equation
assumptions: σ_f = K·εⁿ; K and n are material inputs (cold-working curves).

manufacturing.forging_force.title: Forging force from flow stress and projected area
assumptions: K_f accounts for friction and complex shape (a table input, ~1 for simple upset to ~8 for complex closed-die shapes).

manufacturing.forging_upset_force.title: Flat-die upsetting force with friction (open-die forging)

variables.name: mu
variables.desc: friction coefficient at the die–workpiece interface
variables.label: μ

assumptions: Axisymmetric upsetting between flat dies with Coulomb friction; the bracketed term (1 + 2μr/(3h)) is the friction-hill correction to the frictionless force σ_f·πr². Requires h > 0.

manufacturing.extrusion.title: Extrusion ratio and ideal extrusion pressure
assumptions: Ideal (frictionless, no redundant work) pressure p = σ_f·ln R; real ram pressure is higher.
method_references: Extrusion ratio R = A0/Af; ideal pressure p = σ_f·ln R (recalled)

manufacturing.drawing.title: Wire/bar drawing force and reduction
assumptions: Ideal (frictionless) drawing stress σ_d = σ_f·ln(A0/Af); F = σ_d·Af. Af ≤ A0 required.

manufacturing.drawing_max_reduction.title: Maximum drawing reduction per pass (die stress limit)
assumptions: At the limit the drawing stress equals the allowable die stress σ_allow = σ_f·ln(A0/Af). With σ_allow = σ_f the ideal limit is r_max = 1 − 1/e ≈ 0.632.

manufacturing.bend_allowance.title: Sheet metal bend allowance (arc length at the neutral axis)
assumptions: Neutral axis at K·t from the inside surface (K ≈ 0.33 for common steels; input).

manufacturing.bend_force.title: V-die bending (air bend) force

variables.name: K_b
variables.desc: die opening / force factor (≈1.33 for a V-die)

assumptions: K_b ≈ 1.33 for a V-die with W ≈ 8t (input); force grows as t².

manufacturing.springback.title: Sheet bending springback (constant neutral-axis length)

variables.name: ratio
variables.desc: radius ratio R_i/R_f (≤ 1; smaller = more springback)

assumptions: Elastic-perfectly-plastic bending. The radius recovery is R_i/R_f = 1 − 3x + 4x³ with x = σ_y·R_i/(E·t), and the neutral axis at mid-thickness keeps its length, θ_f/θ_i = (R_i + t/2)/(R_f + t/2). Valid for x < 0.5 (x ≥ 0.5 is a fully elastic bend with no permanent set, which is rejected).
method_references: Springback radius ratio R_i/R_f = 1 − 3(σy Ri/Et) + 4(σy Ri/Et)³ and neutral-axis θ_f/θ_i = (R_i + t/2)/(R_f + t/2) (recalled)

manufacturing.blanking_punching_force.title: Blanking / punching force

variables.name: P_per
variables.desc: sheared perimeter (πD for a round hole)

assumptions: τ_s ≈ 0.7·UTS when only the tensile strength is known (input).
method_references: Blanking force F = perimeter × t × shear strength (recalled)

manufacturing.blanking_clearance.title: Blanking / punching die clearance
assumptions: Typical clearance per side is 3–10% of thickness depending on material (input).

manufacturing.blank_diameter.title: Blank diameter for a cylindrical deep-drawn cup
assumptions: Constant wall thickness, equal surface area (no bottom radius or flange added).

manufacturing.draw_ratio.title: Draw ratio and limiting draw ratio check

variables.name: margin
variables.desc: feasibility margin LDR/DR (≥ 1 = feasible in one draw)

variables.name: LDR
variables.desc: limiting draw ratio (material limit, ≈1.8–2.2 first draw)

assumptions: Feasible in one draw when DR ≤ LDR (margin ≥ 1), else redraw or anneal. LDR is a material input, not computed here.

manufacturing.pattern_dimension.title: Casting pattern dimensions from shrinkage allowance
assumptions: The pattern is made LARGER than the casting (L_p = L_c(1+s)) so the metal shrinks to the desired size. s is the linear shrinkage as a fraction m/m (0.02 for steel, ~0.01 for cast iron; input) — sources quoting mm/m or % must be divided by 1000 or 100 respectively.

manufacturing.chvorinov.title: Chvorinov solidification time
assumptions: t_s = C(V/A)² with the mold constant C as input (order 4·10⁵ s/m² for steel in sand).

manufacturing.riser_sizing.title: Riser modulus and adequacy ratio (cylindrical side riser)

variables.name: ratio
variables.desc: M_r / M_c (≥ 1.2 to feed the casting)

assumptions: Cylindrical side riser (side + both ends cooling): M = DH/(4H + 2D). A top riser (side + top cooling) is DH/(4H + D). Keep ratio ≥ 1.2.
method_references: Riser modulus = V/A; cylindrical side riser M = DH/(4H + 2D) (recalled)

manufacturing.gating_velocity.title: Gating (pouring) velocity from sprue height (Torricelli)

variables.name: h
variables.desc: sprue height (head of metal above the gate)

assumptions: Ideal (loss-free) flow from the pouring basin; real gates use a velocity < this.

manufacturing.weld_heat_input.title: Arc-welding heat input per unit length

variables.name: H
variables.desc: heat input per unit weld length

assumptions: η ≈ 0.7–0.85 for SMAW/GMAW, ~0.9 submerged arc (input).

manufacturing.weld_melting_efficiency.title: Welding melting efficiency

variables.name: eta_m
variables.desc: melting efficiency (energy to melt / heat input)
variables.label: ηm

assumptions: Energy to melt = A_m·ρ·v·(c·ΔT + L_f) (sensible + latent, no superheat); heat input = V·I·η.

manufacturing.weld_cooling_rate.title: Weld cooling rate (3-D thick-plate Rosenthal)

variables.name: H
variables.desc: net heat input per unit length

assumptions: Thick (3-D) plate: R = 2πk(T_c − T_0)²/H. For thin plates the 2-D form R = 2πkρc(t/H)²(T_c − T_0)³ applies instead. Requires T_c > T_0 (there is no cooling at or below the preheat temperature).

manufacturing.injection_clamping_force.title: Injection molding clamping force

variables.name: A_proj
variables.desc: projected area of the part (and runner)

assumptions: Cavity pressure (typically 20–60 MPa for thermoplastics) is an input.

manufacturing.injection_cooling_time.title: Injection molding cooling time (slab conduction)

variables.name: t
variables.desc: cooling time to the ejection temperature

assumptions: First-term (Fourier) solution of a slab cooled from both faces. profile="mean" uses the thickness-averaged temperature with the 8/π² coefficient (T_e is then the MEAN ejection temperature); profile="centreline" uses the mid-plane temperature with the 4/π coefficient. Requires T_m > T_w and T_e > T_w.
method_references: Injection-molding cooling time t = (s²/π²α)·ln[K(T_m − T_w)/(T_e − T_w)] with K = 8/π² (mean) or 4/π (centreline) (recalled)

manufacturing.pm_density.title: Powder-metallurgy green/sintered density
assumptions: Density from mass and volume; relative density = fraction of the pore-free density.

manufacturing.pm_heckel.title: Powder compaction pressure (Heckel equation)
assumptions: Heckel compaction law ln(1/(1−ρ_rel)) = A + K·P; A and K are material inputs.
method_references: Heckel equation ln(1/(1 − ρ_rel)) = A + K·P (recalled)

manufacturing.am_layer_count.title: 3D printing layer count (rounded up to a whole layer)

variables.name: N
variables.desc: number of layers (rounded up to a whole layer)

assumptions: The layer count is rounded UP to a whole number of layers (N = ceil(H/L_t)); H_built = N·L_t is the height actually built, which is ≥ H unless H/L_t is exact.

manufacturing.am_build_time.title: 3D printing build time (extrusion-limited)
assumptions: Extrusion-limited time = volume/(bead area × head speed); travel, acceleration and layer changes add overhead not counted here.

source.derivation: H/L_t = 0.05005/0.0002 = 250.25 → ceil = 251 layers; H_built = 251·0.0002 = 0.0502 m (the 0.05 mm overshoot is the rounded-up half-layer)
